chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali bin Raib, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked (and I was present) about a man who married a woman for one hundred dinars, with the stipulation that she would go with him to his land/country. If she does not go with him, then her dower is fifty dinars, if she refuses to go with him to his land.

He said, so he (peace be upon him) said: If he intends to take her to the land of polytheism, then there is no stipulation valid for him upon her regarding that, and she is entitled to the one hundred dinars which he had dowered for her. And if he intends to take her to the land of the Muslims and the abode of Islam, then he has what he stipulated upon her; and the Muslims are upon their stipulations. And it is not for him to take her to his land until he pays her her dower, or she is pleased with him from that with whatever she is pleased with, and that is permissible for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a marital stipulation requiring a wife to relocate to a non-Muslim country?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies that the validity of relocation stipulations depends on the destination's religious context, voiding the condition if the wife is moved to 'Bald al-Shirk' (land of polytheism) while upholding it for 'Dar al-Islam'. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that 'Muslims are bound by their conditions' (al-Muslimun 'ala shurutihim), provided the condition does not contravene divine law or harm the wife's rights. The hadith also establishes that the husband cannot exercise his right of conjugal cohabitation until the dower is paid or mutually agreed upon, linking financial obligation to marital rights.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked and I was present, about a man who married a woman upon one (a dower of) hundred Dinars upon a stipulation that she would be going out with him to his city.
So if she were not to go out, her dower would be fifty Dinars, if she refuses to go out with him to his city.

The (narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he intends to go out with her to a city of the Polytheism, so there is no (valid) stipulation for him upon her regarding that, and for her would be one hundred Dinars which he had dowered for her; but if he intends to go out with her to a city of the Muslims and a house of Al-Islam, so for him would be whatever he stipulated upon her; and the Muslims are (bound) by their stipulations, and it would not be for him that he goes out with her to his city until he pays here dower to her, or she is pleased from him from that with whatever she is pleased with, and it would be allowed for him’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab who has said the following:

“This is concerning a question before abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in my presence, about the case of a man who marries a woman for one hundred dinar with the condition that she will go with him to his town. If she will not go with him to his town her mahr (dower) will be fifty dinar.

He (the Imam) said, ‘If he wants to take her to the lands of pagans, then such condition is not valid and the one hundred dinar belongs to her which is her mahr (dower) but if he wants to take her to the lands of the Muslims within the Muslim domain then the condition is valid in his favor; Muslims must stand by their conditions. He cannot take her out of her town without first paying her mahr (dower) or make her agree with whatever amount, it then is permissible.’”
